shortlist.raw_text: Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents increasingly act over streaming omni-modal observations spanning screenshots, audio, video, interaction history, and device states. However, exposing this complete context uniformly at every step ignores that relevance is transient and sparse: the signal determining one action can become clutter at the next. Because executed actions feed back into the context, these errors compound into Sequential Distraction, driving the agent into irreversible trajectory drift. We formulate the underlying requirement as Focused Perception: a representation that is step-adaptive, action-sufficient, and non-intrusive. We realize this in FocusGUI, a lightweight adapter that dynamically prioritizes multimodal channels against a step-specific decision reference. Instead of uniformly processing all inputs, it compresses the most relevant evidence into a compact latent and subtly injects it into the frozen decoder's embeddings, guiding the model's attention without altering its native parameter space. FocusGUI trains from action supervision alone, requiring neither modality-relevance labels nor backbone fine-tuning. Across four omni-modal backbones, it raises overall Type Match by +33.2 and Exact Match by 3.0 times over the frozen backbone on average, and Type Match by +30.1 over the strongest existing enhancement method.

shortlist.raw_text: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, Ψ_0, ω-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

shortlist.raw_text: Moving from controllable videos to genuinely playable worlds requires persistent world state, executable game rules, and low-latency interaction. We outline a roadmap for the next generation of Matrix-Game that separates game execution from visual generation through an executable game harness, and introduce Matrix-Game 4.0 as the first system built on this design. A lightweight game engine maintains world state and executes interaction rules, a multimodal coding agent translates player ideas into game code and dynamic scene captions, and a renderer based on autoregressive video model transforms engine-rendered low-poly proxies into detailed visuals, conditioned on dynamic captions and memory references. This framework provides continuous guidance for visual generation and enables natural-language creation and modification of scenes and gameplay. Our renderer is trained on aligned low-poly and high-fidelity video pairs and distilled into a causal generator that generates in four-frame chunks with one or two denoising steps. Together with targeted inference optimizations, Matrix-Game 4.0 enables 480p, 60 FPS gameplay on a single NVIDIA RTX5090 with a key-press-to-display latency of 112ms. Single-step generation achieves 83FPS steady-state throughput with 18.2GiB of peak GPU memory usage. With fixed prompts, steady-state throughput also reaches 67FPS on an RTX5080 and 58FPS on an RTX5070Ti. We demonstrate customizable shooter and driving games with engine-enforced mechanics, and release code, model weights, and low-poly game assets to support research and creation of playable game worlds.

context:
Title: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud

Text:
OpenAI and Google Cloud are bringing frontier models and Codex workflows to Gemini’s Model Garden, available through Google Cloud Marketplace.

Article text (excerpt):
OpenAI and Google Cloud ⁠ (opens in a new window) are partnering to bring OpenAI’s frontier models and Codex ⁠ (opens in a new window) agentic workflows into Google Cloud’s Model Garden. The integration will give customers native access to these models to power complex agentic workflows at scale, backed by Google Cloud’s data governance and high-performance infrastructure.
Google Cloud’s longstanding investment in machine learning and AI has made it a destination for AI workloads and the developers and data scientists building them. Bringing OpenAI models to its model garden gives these teams access to OpenAI’s frontier models within the environment where they already work, enabling enterprises to modernize their software development lifecycle, build agentic workflows, and change how people work.
For organizations in regulated industries, deploying AI requires control over who can access sensitive data and how it is used. The integration will pair OpenAI’s frontier models with Google Cloud’s built-in access controls, centralized data governance, and high-performance infrastructure to support demanding enterprise workloads.
Google Cloud customers will be able to purchase OpenAI frontier models via model garden, transacted through the Google Cloud Marketplace. Enterprises with Google Cloud spend commitments will be able to draw down their GCP commitments for these purchases.
Additionally, OpenAI models will soon be available in Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent, providing enterprise customers with model choice flexibility and the best model for each task. By expanding access through Google Cloud, we are giving enterprises greater choice in how they discover and use frontier models, with a path from evaluation to broader adoption.
General availability is planned in the coming weeks. Request access to OpenAI on Google Cloud here .

Coverage from CNBC: "OpenAI to bring AI models to Google's cloud, in further expansion beyond Microsoft"
OpenAI will make its artificial intelligence models available for developers through Google's cloud, following years of competition between the two companies.
For OpenAI, the effort reflects a growing push to expand distribution of its technology to enterprise developers. That's critical as the ChatGPT creator looks to build its business beyond its consumer roots, and the move puts OpenAI's models on all three of the top cloud infrastructure providers.
Less than six months ago, OpenAI said Microsoft would no longer have the exclusive license on its intellectual property. The day after that ended, cloud leader Amazon unveiled plans to host OpenAI models .
Now Google is getting its shot, bringing OpenAI's GPT products to its cloud's model garden and Antigravity coding tool in the coming weeks.
"Google Cloud's longstanding investment in machine learning and AI has made it a destination for AI workloads and the developers and data scientists building them," OpenAI said in a blog post.
Google has been on a run in cloud computing this year. Annualized revenue growth in the segment accelerated to about 82% in the second quarter from 63% in the first quarter, thanks partly to strong demand for AI models and custom chips. Amazon and Microsoft posted second-quarter cloud growth of 37% and 42% , respectively. All three report quarterly results next week.
Most business spending on AI is on OpenAI and Anthropic, according to data from corporate card issuer Ramp, though some corporate IT departments have integrated Google's Gemini models into their systems. In September, Google announced its next-generation Gemini 4 Argon model.
OpenAI was founded in 2015 partly as a counterweight to the concentration of AI research at companies like Google. Two years later, Google employees submitted the influential Transformer academic paper that propelled AI, but it was OpenAI that helped bring the technology forward with ChatGPT. Now OpenAI is courting investors at a $1.4 trillion valuation and targeting an initial public offering.
Google and OpenAI previously partnered last year, when the AI lab said it was using Google's cloud to run ChatGPT and its application programming interface.

Coverage from The Hindu BusinessLine: "OpenAI partners with Google Cloud to offer AI models, codex workflows"
Sam Altman-led OpenAI has partnered with Google Cloud to make its advanced AI models and Codex agentic workflows available through Google Cloud's Model Garden, according to a statement by the ChatGPT maker.
The partnership will allow enterprises to develop and deploy AI-powered workflows using Google Cloud's infrastructure and data governance capabilities.
“OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud. We're bringing our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud's Model Garden, so enterprises can use our technology where they already build,” the AI giant said in an X post.
Google Cloud customers will be able to purchase OpenAI's AI models through Model Garden via the Google Cloud Marketplace. Customers with existing Google Cloud Platform (GCP) spending commitments will also be able to use those commitments for these purchases.OpenAI models will also soon be available on Google Antigravity and the Gemini Agent, giving enterprise customers more options to select models based on their specific tasks and requirements.
The partnership aims to expand access to OpenAI's models and help businesses integrate them into their existing workflows, the company said. “By expanding access through Google Cloud, we are giving enterprises greater choice in how they discover and use frontier models, with a path from evaluation to broader adoption,” the company said.
Commenting on the development, Greg Brockman, President and co-founder, OpenAI, said, “Google Cloud is a leading platform for developers and businesses building AI agents, writing software, and putting AI to work. This partnership is an important step in making our most capable models and Codex available where customers are already building, giving them even more choice in how they use frontier AI as we grow the agentic ecosystem together.”
Thomas Kurian, Chief Executive Officer, Google Cloud, added, “We are focused on giving customers a broad selection of models, including those from OpenAI, so they can choose the right model for any given job, helping to deliver optimal quality and lower costs.”

Background (Garden city movement, Wikipedia):
The garden city movement is a 20th-century urban planning movement that promoted satellite communities surrounding a central city, separated by green belts. These garden cities would contain proportionate areas of residences, industry, and agriculture. Ebenezer Howard first posited the idea in 1898 as a way to capture the primary benefits of the countryside and the city while avoiding the disadvantages presented by both. In the early 20th century, Letchworth and Welwyn Garden City were built near London according to Howard's concept, and many other garden cities inspired by his model have since been built all over the world.

Background (AI agent, Wikipedia):
An AI agent is an artificial intelligence program that can make decisions, pursue goals, and take actions independently of human programmers. Agentic AI contrasts with tool-like AI use for narrow, specific tasks such as answering questions - as with chatbots in the non-agentic forms that were common in 2023, or with traditional machine learning algorithms.

text:
Enterprise buyers are fundamentally changing how they procure AI infrastructure.

Less than six months after ending its exclusive deal with Microsoft, OpenAI is bringing its frontier models and Codex workflows to Google Cloud.

The tools will launch in Google Cloud's Model Garden, Google Cloud Marketplace, the Antigravity coding tool, and the Gemini Agent.

The procurement mechanics are what matter most here. Enterprise customers will not need new vendor contracts or separate billing setups. Instead, they can draw down existing Google Cloud spend commitments to pay for OpenAI access.

This move puts OpenAI across all three major cloud providers. Corporate card data from Ramp shows OpenAI and Anthropic currently capture most business AI spending. At the same time, Google Cloud annualized revenue growth accelerated to about 82% in the second quarter, up from 63% in the first quarter.

By hosting rival models on its own rails, Google captures platform spend without forcing enterprise customers to use Gemini for every task.

Cloud exclusivity is dead. Infrastructure providers now have to host their direct competitors just to keep existing corporate budgets from walking out the door.

Source: OpenAI, with reporting from CNBC and The Hindu BusinessLine

#CloudComputing #AI
alt_openings:
1. Bare number first
Line 1: An 82% cloud growth rate wasn't enough to keep Google from hosting OpenAI.
Line 2: OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud, allowing enterprise buyers to pay for GPT access using existing Google spending commitments.
Prefer this when writing for finance, sales, or strategy executives who judge platform shifts by financial performance.

2. Tool as subject
Line 1: OpenAI just put its frontier models onto all three major cloud providers.
Line 2: A new integration brings OpenAI models and Codex tools directly into Google Cloud's Model Garden and Marketplace.
Prefer this when targeting general engineers and product managers who care primarily about model distribution and availability.

3. Your X
Line 1: Your enterprise Google Cloud budget can now pay for OpenAI models.
Line 2: OpenAI is bringing its models and Codex workflows directly into Google Cloud Marketplace, drawing down existing commitment spend.
Prefer this when targeting IT decision-makers, CTOs, and procurement leaders who manage cloud commit budgets directly.

Pick: The "Your X" opening. It speaks directly to enterprise leaders who hold GCP spend commitments, instantly showing them a practical financial shortcut before they even tap "see more."
firewall_notes: "Six months after dropping Microsoft exclusivity, OpenAI just landed on Google Cloud." — Gives away the entire news payoff in the first line before the reader hits the fold.
"That puts its models on all three major cloud platforms—and lets enterprises buy them..." — Uses an unnecessary em dash to fuse two separate analytical points.
"• Model Garden and Google Cloud Marketplace / • The Antigravity coding tool / • The Gemini Agent" — Relies on a mechanical bulleted triad that disrupts prose flow.
"My read: cloud exclusivity is officially dead." — Uses lazy, self-referential conversational filler ("My read").
"Which cloud platform is your team using for AI workloads today?" — Ends on a generic engagement-bait question instead of a firm analytical landing.
